text:
incident-bot: PROD alert — continuous-batch pool 'cb-eu-west-1' reporting KV cache size spike and increased tail latency across serving nodes. Errors: 5025 cache eviction errors in last 5m. Severity: P2.

maya (oncall): seeing huge paging churn on the kvcache. latency p95 jumped from 85ms -> 700ms on several replicas. Noticed `max_batch_tokens` is 65536 in the cluster config.

cheng: ugh that value is insane for this workload. default recommended is 8k-16k. Did a recent rollout change that? @deploy-bot any deploys to cb-config in last hour?

deploy-bot: deploy cb-config v2.9.1 promoted to cb-eu-west-1 at 1978001820 by emily (platform). No rollback performed.

alex: paging thrash + large batches => huge KV cache growth because prefetching/kv paging keeps touching many pages per request. That will blow the backing storage and cause eviction storms. We should reduce `max_batch_tokens` and `max_num_seqs` ASAP and force continuous-batching to fallback mode.

maya (oncall): agree. I'm going to apply an emergency hotfix to tier-1 pool: lower `max_batch_tokens` to 12000 and `max_num_seqs` to 8, and set `continuous_batching.enabled=false` for that pool. Will patch via `kubectl patch` to configmap.

cheng: call out the exact commands so SRE can run them if maya gets paged out: 
```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap cb-pool-cb-eu-west --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_batch_tokens":"12000","max_num_seqs":"8","continuous_batching":"false"}}'
# then rollout restart the serving pods
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/cb-runtime-eu-west
```

alex: also bump request timeout to 30s for that pool temporarily to avoid cascading client retries: `request_timeout_ms=30000` in the same configmap.

sophia (cs): heads up — we've got 2 paying customers hitting degraded responses (search team and chat app). CS is pinging them and offering status. No data loss reported but higher latency and some 5xx.

maya (oncall): applying patch now. I'll push to one node first then do rolling.

maya (oncall): (after) patched configmap and restarted 2/6 pods. Monitoring KV cache size and tail latency.

alex: watching metrics — eviction rate dropped ~40% on the restarted pods, p95 latency fell to ~220ms there. Good sign.

deploy-bot: rollback request? There is no full rollback for cb-config; we patched live.

cheng: fine for emergency. Next step: if evictions continue on remaining pods, we'll scale down continuous-batching worker threads to force per-request batching. Also prepare a quick revert playbook to restore previous throughput settings once KV stabilizes.

maya (oncall): remaining pods restarting. TTL for client-side retries temporarily increased to avoid re-flooding.

jun (oncall-next): stepping in for handoff in 10. What should I watch?

maya (oncall): monitor these dashboards: `cb_eu_kv_cache_total_pages`, `cb_eu_eviction_rate`, `cb_eu_batch_size_p95`, `cb_eu_latency_p95`. If eviction_rate > 1000/min or p95 > 500ms, escalate immediately. Also watch ingress errors per-customer.

emily (platform): creating an emergency runbook entry and adding the hotfix patch snippet. Also opening a temporary feature flag to disable continuous batching per-customer if needed.

alex: note: follow-up action item — analyze recent config rollouts: who changed `max_batch_tokens` to 65536. That should have been gated. Add a validation to disallow values > 20000 for managed pools.

maya (oncall): CS reported one of the customers saw ~10% 5xx during the incident window. Sophia, what's their tolerance?

sophia (cs): we've offered credits and will do a deeper impact call if they want. Logged case and notifying account team.

cheng: for root cause, suspect two things combined: bad config increase and a workload shift with longer sequences increasing the effective token footprint -> more KV pages per request. Paging thrash is non-linear. We'll add better sampling of sequence-length histograms into the console.

maya (oncall): current status: all pods rolled, eviction rate down 82% cluster-wide, latency p95 stabilized at ~180ms. Marking incident as mitigated.

jun (oncall-next): taking over as oncall. I'll keep monitoring for 1 hour and then start cleanup: revert request_timeout_ms to default, and plan a controlled re-test for increasing batching ceiling with canary traffic.

emily (platform): creating follow-up ticket: #INF-1427 - "config guardrails: max_batch_tokens upper bound, rollout validation, console histogram for seq lengths". Assigning to cheng + alex.

alex: let's schedule a postmortem and include the customer impact summary, timeline, and the config validation patch. Aim for a writeup within 48 hours.

sophia (cs): I'll compile the customer impact notes and timelines for the case owners.

incident-bot: Incident P2 - cb-eu-west-1 KV cache/paging mitigated. Duration: ~27m. Actions: emergency patch (reduce max_batch_tokens, max_num_seqs), restart pods, increased request timeout, CS notified. Follow-up tickets created.

maya (oncall): handoff complete to jun. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
